justification: The staircase that moved last week does not need moving again. George Pickens was given a part to play against Tony's team and he played it — thirty-eight points is not luck, it is a door that was always going to open, and a man does not close a door the moment it has proven useful merely because another door now looks tidier. Garrett Wilson sheds his cloak of "Questionable" this week and sits a while longer still; forgiveness for a disappointing man comes easily in this house, but so does patience for one whose moment simply has not arrived. Jonathan Taylor, Tyler Warren, and Spencer Shrader have already played their Friday hand against Houston and need no further tending from me. Chris Rodriguez Jr. holds the second running spot, not because the garden behind him has bloomed — Emanuel Wilson rests Out, and the rest of that bed is Seattle's quiet week, not mine — but because there is nothing yet worth disturbing him for. Denver, Daniels, Olave, and Washington stand as they stood. The box score will say what it says; I am reading for what has not happened yet.
